videos.title: MCP: The 'USB-C for AI', Explained (Model Context Protocol)
videos.description:
On its own, an AI model is brilliant but sealed off — it can’t open your files, read your code, or touch your tools. For a while we fixed that by hand: a custom connector for every app times every tool, a tangle that never scaled. MCP — the Model Context Protocol — replaces that mess with one open standard. Think USB-C, but for AI and the tools it uses.

This is MCP explained from scratch, no hype. You’ll see why a raw model is a “mind with no hands,” how the old M×N integration tangle collapses into one clean connection, and the two simple roles that make it work: a client (the AI app) and a server (a small program that wraps a tool or data source) — both speaking the same protocol. We cover what a server actually offers (tools, resources, and prompts), the live request→tool→result loop, why the ecosystem caught on so fast, how MCP differs from plain tool-calling, and the one honest catch: real reach means real trust.

If you’ve wondered how assistants and coding tools suddenly started using your apps and data, this is the plumbing underneath it.

videos.description:
On-device AI just crossed a real threshold. PrismML's Bonsai 27B squeezes a 27-billion-parameter multimodal model down to 3.9GB — small enough to run natively on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, no cloud required. It's a 1-bit build of Qwen3.6-27B trained low-bit from the start (not quantized after the fact), with a 262K context window, vision, and tool calling. A laptop-class ternary version (5.9GB) is also out, both under Apache 2.0. The pitch: agentic workloads that run hundreds of local steps at zero marginal cost, with your data never leaving the device. Trade-offs exist — tool-calling accuracy drops at 1-bit and some benchmarks are contested — so test before you ship.
